neighbours.label: electric motor and drive engineering terms (' frequency' in variable/adjustable-frequency drive, ' motor', rotating magnetic ' field')
fire: The new pumping station runs on variable frequency drives to save energy.
Each conveyor is powered by a three-phase induction motor rated at 30 kW.
Adjustable-frequency drives let the fans slow down when demand is low.
The synchronous motor turns because the stator creates a rotating magnetic field.
Engineers replaced the old motor starters with soft starters last year.
The motor must be rated for both motor and generator operation in this design.
A variable frequency drive changes the speed of the motor by changing the supply frequency.
The compressor is driven by a large electric motor bolted to the base frame.
quiet: The new pumping station uses larger storage tanks to save space.
Each conveyor carries crates of apples from the orchard to the packing shed.
Wider ducts let the air move quietly when the building is full.
The tall chimney releases warm air because the furnace heats the room below.
Engineers replaced the old wooden walkways with steel grating last year.
The tank must be rated for both hot and cold water storage in this design.
A pressure gauge shows the operator how full the boiler is during the shift.
The compressor housing is painted yellow and bolted to the concrete floor.

notes: Card top: variable/adjustable ' frequency' drives (53.75, 49.75), ' motor' x4, ' control', rotating magnetic ' field'. Near misses keep industrial plant/pump context without motors or drives.
